info.title: Suplex AgentApi Runtime API
info.description: Version v1 is additive-only within a major version. Pairing, credential rotation, and administration are separate provisioning APIs and are not part of this contract. Company, project grants, and creator ownership come from current server persistence, never request fields. Reads cover every task in the agent's currently granted projects. Commands, dependency writes, and delivery operations remain creator-only. Denied company, grant, and missing-resource reads are all non-enumerating 404 responses.

post.summary: Create a backlog or queued task
post.description: Creates a backlog task. With queue true, the task is queued: it starts now when every prerequisite is complete, and otherwise stays queued with zero sessions until the last prerequisite completes. Without queue, it never starts by itself. dryRun true validates the same request and returns its projection without writing a task, dependency, receipt, artifact, or audit event. The server defaults description to an empty string and rejects unknown fields with request_invalid. dependsOn sets the prerequisites, shown as Blocked by. A prerequisite can be any task the agent can read in a granted project. The task waits for the prerequisite. Reading a prerequisite gives no commands on it. A self-reference, a cycle, or a task outside a granted project is rejected. Idempotency is scoped to the paired agent and company. An identical replay returns 200; reuse for a different request returns 409 with idempotency_conflict. GET /api/agent/tasks supports opaque cursors and returns nextCursor.

blockedByPullRequests.description: Pull requests in the project repository. Suplex observes each one before saving it. An open pull request blocks until it merges. A closed pull request blocks until it is reopened and merged or removed.

queue.description: Queue the task: it starts now when every prerequisite is complete, and otherwise starts by itself when the last one completes. Without it, the task stays in the manual backlog.

get.summary: Read a task in a granted project
get.description: A paired agent can read every task in its currently granted company projects. A task created by another actor reports permittedCommands as an empty array. Task states are backlog, queued, active, waiting_human, cancelled, and delivered. queue.waitingOn lists the exact wait reason of each incomplete prerequisite. A prerequisite is complete when it is delivered at its own delivery target; the merged target also needs the merged pull request state Suplex observed from GitHub. Human questions are records only: answering them remains human authority and no agent answer command exists. The server router rejects path parameters longer than 100 characters before this authenticated operation is matched; those router-level responses are outside this contract.

put.summary: Replace the prerequisites of a task
put.description: Replaces dependsOn, shown as Blocked by, with the complete set in the body. A prerequisite can be any task the agent can read in a granted project. The task waits for the prerequisite. Reading a prerequisite gives no commands on it. A self-reference, a cycle, or a task outside a granted project is rejected. dryRun true validates the replacement and reports the projected prerequisites and start state without changing dependencies, queue state, or audits. A self-reference, a cycle, or an unavailable task is rejected and the current set stays. Unknown fields are rejected. The response and every later read report dependsOn and blockedBy from the same stored edges.

dependsOn.description: A prerequisite can be any task the agent can read in a granted project. The task waits for the prerequisite. Reading a prerequisite gives no commands on it. A self-reference, a cycle, or a task outside a granted project is rejected. The complete set replaces the current set; an empty array removes every prerequisite.

post.summary: Apply an authorized task lifecycle command
post.description: Only the paired agent that created the task can send a command. Every command requires the current task revision and an idempotency key. start_task queues a manual backlog task: it starts now when every prerequisite is complete and never bypasses one. disarm_task returns a queued task to the manual backlog. taskCommands lists exactly the lifecycle commands accepted by suplex_command_task. autonomousCommands also includes task creation and, when enabled, runtime delivery commands. Human answers remain unavailable to paired agents. The runtime API exposes delivery and merge commands only when capabilities reports them. Suplex can perform delivery for a task's configured target, including a merge after review, without an agent command.
